mechanism_claims.claim_text: Pa-MAP 1.9 directly permeabilized anionic lipid vesicles in carboxyfluorescein leakage assays, with much weaker leakage from zwitterionic/cholesterol-containing vesicles under the tested range.
direct_assay_types: carboxyfluorescein leakage assay with large unilamellar vesicles
mechanism_claims.limitations: Quantitative curve values are figure-based; final curation preserves concentration thresholds stated in text rather than digitizing plots.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AFM imaging supports dose-dependent E. coli surface perturbation: slight roughness at 6 μM and stronger surface disruption at 300 μM.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source explicitly frames intracellular targets as possible at lower concentration; AFM alone is not treated as proof of a single lytic mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD, molecular dynamics, docking, and Table 2 support an amphipathic alpha-helical structure and stronger modeled interaction with anionic POPC/POPS membranes than cholesterol-rich zwitterionic membranes.
mechanism_claims.limitations: In silico docking/dynamics are treated as supporting context, not direct biological mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Biofilm inhibition is supported as an activity phenotype, with MBIC values in Table 1 and flow-cell images, but it is not promoted to a quorum-sensing or biofilm-specific molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Pa-MAP 1.9 against E. coli and K. pneumoniae biofilms
mechanism_claims.limitations: No unsupported quorum-sensing or intracellular-target claim is asserted from the local material.

quality_cautions: Figure curves were not digitized; only text-supported concentration statements and table values were curated.
Computational membrane interaction evidence is not promoted to direct mechanism.
